lawRefs: N.D.C.C. § 57-38-30.3 (rates, indexing, adjustments incl. 40% net long-term capital gain exclusion and Social Security subtraction)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Brackets are the '2026 Forms ND-1 and ND-EZ Tax Rate Schedules' printed in the 2026 Form ND-1ES (SFN 28709, 12-2025); Tax Foundation's January 2026 table shows 2025 widths. North Dakota starts from FEDERAL TAXABLE INCOME, so the federal standard deduction (2026: $16,100 single / $32,200 MFJ, plus federal age 65+ amounts) or itemized deductions are already embedded: standardDeduction, personalExemption and seniorExtraDeduction are 0 here. Zero-rate band up to $49,575 single, $82,800 MFJ, $41,400 MFS, $66,400 HOH; 1.95% to $250,400 / $304,850 / $152,425 / $277,600; 2.5% above. 40% of net long-term capital gain is excluded (2025 Form ND-1 instructions). Taxable Social Security benefits are fully subtracted. No general pension/IRA exclusion. A marriage penalty credit is available to some two-earner joint filers.

flags.standardDeduction: 0 because the state starts from federal taxable income (federal standard/itemized deduction embedded)
